purpose: Teach: 高まり/渡さ/覆わ/広まっ/害する/根ざし/崩す/利か

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、注目度の高まりを論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: Sakura, you handled the topic of growing attention in your paper, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, measured opening. Gentle confirmation—not interrogating, genuinely recalling. Soft eye contact, teacher-to-student respect. Even pace, slightly thoughtful pause before her name.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、文化を渡さない政策を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I wrote about policies that don't allow culture to be transmitted.
lines.style: Clear, direct answer with quiet conviction. Slight lift on the opening affirmation. No performance, just precision. Voice steady, almost relieved to say it plainly.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 森に覆われた地域を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: And you explored forest-covered regions in your work, didn't you?
lines.style: Thoughtful, slightly slower. Not accusatory—curious, following the thread. A beat before 'forest,' like she's recognizing the shift in scope. Gentle confirmation again.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、世界に広まった俳句を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I focused on haiku and how it spread across the world.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact, but with quiet pride underneath. Direct connection to the question. No hesitation, voice settled. Slight warmth on 'world,' acknowledging the scope.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 環境を害する行為を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: So you also examined harmful environmental practices in your paper?
lines.style: Slight shift—more active listening, drawing her out. Engaged but not leading. A touch of recognition that this is a bigger picture emerging. Steady, encouraging tone.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、地域に根ざした文化を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I wrote about culture that's rooted deeply in its region.
lines.style: Same steady voice, but with a small note of resilience. She's answering the thread she sees, not the one the teacher hints at. Grounded, assured. No defensiveness.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 社会通念を崩す思想を論文で扱っていましたね
lines.en: Your paper addressed ideas that challenge conventional thinking, didn't it?
lines.style: Slower, more reflective. Teacher is seeing the full picture now. Respectful pause before 'ideas.' Recognition in her tone—this is bigger than she initially framed it. Warm, not patronizing.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、規制が利かない海域を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I examined unregulated waters and what happens there.
lines.style: Closing answer with quiet finality. Voice doesn't trail—it settles. She's said what she needed to say. Composed, self-assured. A small note of resolution, not apology.
